To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
embarrassment is characterized by a neural network of mentalizing and arousal processing systems and that this embarrassment network is modulated by social anxiety.
the neural underpings of embarrassment are located within the (para-) limbic system.
the neural pathways of social embarrassment include the ventral anterior cingulate and insular cortex and that social anxiety modulates the neural pathways of embarrassing moments.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question how social anxiety affects the neural processing of embarrassing situations.
the neurocognitive mechanisms underlying the experience of embarrassment.
the neural underpining of social anxiety.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
embarrassment can be induced by failures and that the experience of embarrassment is associated with activations of the mentalizing network as well as of arousal processing systems.

embarrassment is a social emotion that is associated with an increased activation of mentalizing areas, arousal processing systems, and the ventral anterior cingulate cortex (ACC), and that social anxiety modulates these processes in a specific manner.
embarrassment is a complex social emotion that is associated with a specific set of neural markers and can be induced in the lab by using a mock-up scenario of person-group interactions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the brain regions that are involved in processing the emotional experience of embarrassment in the context of social anxiety are the same regions that are involved when people are processing the emotions of other people.
social anxiety is a disorder of social cognition and that the neural correlates of embarrassment are a promising target for treatment.
social anxiety disorders may be conceptualized as an exaggerated embarrassment response.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the neural pathways of shame and embarrassment can be identified and that the brain activity during these aversive social moments can be modulated by social anxiety.
embarrassment is a genuine emotion that can be induced in the laboratory and that the neural underpings of embarrassment can be characterized.
the brain's embarrassment pathways may be targeted in treatment strategies for social phobia.
